note: On paper the best-qualified prospect in the batch — runs a hedge fund, was last week deciding between $2.2bn and $2.25bn on a single asset package, describes himself as 'well-to-do', and is explicitly maintain-and-improve rather than rescue. He is nowhere near the excluded deconditioned profile: 66, trains five times a week for an hour, walks 15-20 km for fun. He fails on the one criterion the ICP is actually built around, and fails it from above: health is not his neglected area, it is his most attended one. That is the whole reason the deal died. The stated ICP screens for someone whose health has slipped while their career succeeded, and it has no language for a successful buyer who is already doing the work — for whom the offer is an upgrade rather than a rescue, and therefore competes on measurable delta rather than on urgency. Worth pairing with the Andrew Clarke call in the same batch: both are edge cases where the miss is that health is under control, and both were lost.
